What It Means: A program that keeps running continuously in the background, independent of any terminal window being open
In This Context: How Hermes typically runs when deployed on Railway or a VPS — it never stops, even if you close your laptop

What It Means: Cloud hosting setups: Railway is a managed app-hosting platform; VPS (Virtual Private Server) is a rented remote Linux machine
In This Context: Where Hermes commonly lives when it's not running on your local Mac

What It Means: A single command-line session window within your terminal app (e.g., macOS Terminal, iTerm2)
In This Context: You just need any tab — doesn't matter which — as long as it can reach Hermes

What It Means: The command-line interface — the set of hermes commands you type to control the agent (start, stop, approve, etc.)
In This Context: The tool you use to interact with Hermes from the terminal

What It Means: Opening a command-line session inside the specific machine/container where Hermes is actually running
In This Context: Needed because your local terminal isn't where Hermes lives — you must connect to the remote machine first

What It Means: A protocol/command (ssh user@host) that lets you remotely log into another computer's terminal securely
In This Context: How you "enter" your Railway project or VPS from your own Mac's terminal

What It Means: Running a program so it occupies and blocks that terminal tab — you can't type other commands in that same tab while it runs
In This Context: What happens if Hermes is started with a plain hermes start command without daemonizing it

What It Means: The terminal tab becomes unusable for anything else because the running process has taken it over
In This Context: Direct consequence of foreground mode — you're stuck watching logs, can't type new commands

What It Means: Opening an entirely separate terminal instance alongside the first
In This Context: Necessary workaround when Hermes is in foreground mode, so you have one tab running Hermes and another free to type commands

What It Means: A specific Hermes CLI command (likely hermes approve or similar) used to confirm/authorize a pending action, like a Telegram bot connection
In This Context: The action you need to run without interrupting Hermes itself

What It Means: A terminal feature (built into iTerm2, tmux, Warp, etc.) that divides one window into two independently usable sections
In This Context: An alternative to opening a whole new window — lets you run Hermes in one half and the approve command in the other

What It Means: Running one command right after another in the exact same terminal tab, sequentially (not simultaneously)
In This Context: Only viable when nothing is running yet — you start Hermes, it does its startup work, then you immediately run approve before it starts blocking
